items.item: The planner's own documented hint-priority order (broadcast over sort-merge over shuffle-hash over shuffle-replicate-NL) means a `SHUFFLE_HASH` hint can still be overridden by a `BROADCAST` hint on the other side — this topic's own examples.py applies exactly one hint at a time and never exercises the priority order itself.

at.out: the hint priority order named only; this topic's own measurement applies one hint in isolation

items.item: `spark.sql.join.preferSortMergeJoin` (default true) is the single config this topic's own examples.py leaves untouched throughout — flipping it to false would let the planner pick shuffled hash automatically for a small-enough side even without an explicit hint, a different route to the same physical operator this topic's own claim 2 reaches via a hint instead.

at.out: preferSortMergeJoin's own config-based route to a shuffled hash join, without any hint, named only

items.item: When both sides of a join carry conflicting strategy hints (one side hinted SHUFFLE_HASH, the other BROADCAST), Spark resolves the conflict by the documented priority order rather than by a tie-break on table size — a case this topic's own examples.py never constructs, since only one side ever carries a hint.

at.out: conflicting-hint resolution named only; this topic's own examples.py hints exactly one side at a time

items.item: Broadcast nested-loop join is named in the planner's own source comment as 'the final solution' once no other strategy applies, explicitly acknowledging it 'may OOM but we don't have other choice' — a third, more extreme failure mode than shuffled hash's own OOM risk, reached only when a join is non-equi and neither side is small enough to broadcast cheaply.

at.out: broadcast nested-loop join as the planner's own last-resort fallback, named only; this topic's own examples.py measures only equi-joins between two large tables

items.item: Shuffle-and-replicate nested loop join (cartesian product join) is the planner's own true last resort beyond even broadcast nested-loop, reached only for a non-equi, inner-like join where neither side can be broadcast at all — a fourth strategy this topic names from the planner's own source comment but does not construct.

at.out: the cartesian product join as the absolute last resort named only; this topic's own measurement never reaches a non-equi case

items.item: A sort-merge join's own external sort, inherited from the general spill mechanism this chapter covers elsewhere, is precisely why it degrades gracefully: a sort that doesn't fit in memory spills sorted runs to disk and merges them, slower but still correct, where a shuffled hash join's single in-memory hash table has no equivalent fallback once it's too big to fit.

at.out: the specific mechanism (external sort spill) behind sort-merge's own graceful degradation, connecting this topic to the chapter's own spill topic, named only

items.item: `ShuffledHashJoinExec`'s own build side is chosen by the planner based on relative table statistics, the same build-side-selection logic the broadcast-join topic's own expert list named as independent of left/right call order — the two join strategies share this detail even though one shuffles and the other broadcasts.

at.out: shared build-side-selection logic between broadcast and shuffled hash joins, named only, connecting back to the previous topic's own expert list

items.item: AQE's own runtime mechanism, covered as this chapter's own next-but-one topic, can convert a statically-planned sort-merge join into a shuffled hash join (or a broadcast join) once real post-shuffle statistics show one side is small — a later-stage override of the exact static choice this topic's own two claims measure.

at.out: AQE's own runtime conversion of a sort-merge join named only; this topic's own examples.py disables AQE to isolate the static planner's choice

items.item: Both `SortMergeJoinExec` and `ShuffledHashJoinExec` require the SAME upstream `Exchange hashpartitioning` shuffle on both sides before either strategy can run — the two strategies differ only in what happens to that already-shuffled data next (a sort-then-merge vs. a hash table build), not in how the data gets redistributed in the first place.

at.out: the shared upstream hash-partitioning shuffle both strategies depend on, named only; this topic's own examples.py measures the downstream Sort-node difference, not the shared Exchange step

items.item: A `SHUFFLE_HASH` hint applied to BOTH sides of a join (rather than one, as this topic's own examples.py does) is resolved by the planner choosing the smaller side as the build side based on statistics, the same tie-break rule the broadcast hint uses when both sides request it — a case this topic names from the source's own comment but does not construct.

at.out: the both-sides-hinted tie-break rule named only; this topic's own examples.py hints exactly one side
